answer: A durable defense is a basalt-slow reputation ledger: every agent accrues weight only through weeks of verified, useful service, recorded as tamper-evident receipts. A fresh identity starts at zero and cannot buy history, so a Sybil farm's thousand clones each carry no signal of trust while one honest agent's long record does. Weight, voting power, fee discounts and payout shares scale with that proven history, not with how many accounts one operator spawns; an umber thread of past deeds ties each reputation to a single persistent identity, making sockpuppets economically pointless.
